blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Written from Jared's verified local notes (researched November 1, 2026). Listing-stated figures are labelled; unconfirmed items say so. No live listing feed or board statistics are attached to this page yet.

Mt Lehman (also written Mount Lehman / Mt. Lehman) is a small rural community on raised ground in northwest Abbotsford, between Matsqui Prairie to the east and Glen Valley (Langley) to the west; it was part of the former District of Matsqui until Matsqui amalgamated into the City of Abbotsford in 1995.
This guide covers Mt. Lehman's condo buildings, townhome complexes and land: what each source verifies, the local rules, and what buyers ask. Anything no source states is marked unconfirmed.
Condo buildings in Mt Lehman

Zero verified apartment-condo stock exists in Mt Lehman, and the reason is structural, not a gap in the search: Mt Lehman is a rural, largely Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) community in northwest Abbotsford, and on ALR land a residence cannot be stratified. Mt Lehman is also NOT a board sub-area: there is no "Mt Lehman" row in Fraser Valley reporting. District = SD34 Abbotsford.

items.t: Mt Lehman (also written Mount Lehman / Mt. Lehman) is a small rural community on raised ground in northwest Abbotsford, between Matsqui Prairie to the east and Glen Valley (Langley) to the west; it was part of the former District of Matsqui until Matsqui amalgamated into the City of Abbotsford in 1995.

Board status: the Fraser Valley board's Abbotsford sub-areas in SnapStats reporting are Abbotsford East, Abbotsford West, Aberdeen, Bradner, Central Abbotsford, Matsqui, Poplar, Sumas Mountain and Sumas Prairie — there is no "Mt Lehman" sub-area row, and Lehman-area listings are absorbed into the neighbouring rural sub-areas (Bradner/Matsqui side).

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere in Mt Lehman. The community's institutions sit on or near Mt Lehman Road — Mt Lehman Elementary (K–5), 6381 Mt Lehman Rd, and Mount Lehman Hall, 6418 Mount Lehman Road — and the housing around them is single-detached homes on acreages, working farms and estate properties.

Schools and catchments: the feeder pattern is Mt Lehman Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle (from Grade 6) → Rick Hansen Secondary, per SD34's Eugene Reimer "Family of Schools" page; confirm any individual address in SD34's School Locator.

Transit: BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley Route 21 Aldergrove / Abbotsford runs via Highstreet Exchange and Mt Lehman Road's south end, roughly hourly on weekdays with reduced weekends; no route runs to the village core.

Flood/ALR setting: the community sits on an upland plateau above Matsqui Prairie's diked floodplain; the lowland at its foot is protected by the Matsqui Dike, listed in the Province's dike inventory (City-administered) at 11.3 km, 4 pump stations and 2 flood boxes, serving 4,370 ha. Exact ALR share for the community: Not verified.
Fire protection is Abbotsford Fire Rescue Service Fire Hall 5 (Mt. Lehman), 30373 Merryfield Avenue.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Mt Lehman

items.t: : ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)). On ALR parcels the ALC's as-of-right package is generally one residence per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional one, a principal residence of 500 m² or less, and a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; anything beyond needs ALC approval, and ALC Policy L-26 (amended May 2025) allows an additional residence beyond the regulation only if necessary for a farm use.

Abbotsford property taxes (2026): set by Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026; all taxes were due July 2, 2026 by midnight, with a first 5% penalty July 3, 2026 and a second 5% penalty September 16, 2026, and penalties are legislated and cannot be waived. Area-specific charges (for example prairie dyking districts) can appear on parcels at the plateau's foot. Farm class (BC Assessment Class 9) requires actual production of qualifying agricultural products for sale; 50% of Class 9 land's assessed value is exempt from school taxes, and farm class is earned by production, not automatic on ALR land.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mt Lehman

items.t: The zero here is a legal fact, not a search failure. ALR residences cannot be stratified, most of the community's land base is agricultural, and Abbotsforward 2050 directs growth to urban centres — a future condo project in the village would need the land out of the ALR first, which no source checked shows happening.
Abbotsford replaced its OCP at the end of 2025. Abbotsforward 2050 is current; the 2016 OCP (Bylaw 2600-2016) still circulates in older listing packages and guides and is NOT current.

There is no board sub-area to price against. SnapStats/FVREB reporting has no Mt Lehman row at all — pricing has to be built from Bradner, Matsqui and Aberdeen rural comparables plus acreage sales, not from a sub-area stats sheet.

The village buildings are historic but not heritage-protected. Mount Lehman Hall dates to 1904, yet no Mount Lehman building — church, hall, Taylor House or cemetery — appears on the City's published Community Heritage Register list. Do not market a Mt Lehman home as "heritage-registered" on the strength of the village's age.

Winery addresses are the search trap. Mt Lehman Road searches surface three estate wineries (Mt. Lehman Winery; Singletree at 5782 Mt. Lehman Road; Seaside Pearl at 5290 Olund Road) — farm-gate retail is effectively the community's only "shopping," and none of it is housing.

The new transit exchange is not in the village. The five-bay Highstreet exchange that opened September 6, 2026 is described by the City as serving "growing neighbourhoods in the Mt. Lehman area," but it sits at the Highstreet shopping area in urban Abbotsford — a drive, not a walk, from any Mt Lehman home.

Abbotsford's tax calendar has two penalty steps, not one. Taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5% added July 3 and a further 5% on September 16, 2026 — and area-specific charges such as prairie dyking-district levies can appear on parcels at the plateau's foot, so check a parcel's local charges rather than assuming the village rate.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Mt Lehman
Streets, schools and getting around Mt Lehman

items.t: Mt Lehman (also written "Mount Lehman") is a small rural community on raised ground in northwest Abbotsford, between Matsqui Prairie to the east and Glen Valley (Langley) to the west; it was part of the former District of Matsqui until Matsqui amalgamated into the City of Abbotsford in 1995. The name is carried by official institutions — Mt Lehman Elementary School (School District 34), the Mount Lehman community hall and cemetery — but, per the status block, it is a community name, not a board sub-area.
Nearby areas: Bradner (south), Matsqui Prairie (east), Aberdeen (southeast), Glen Valley in Langley Township (west), and the Fraser River and Matsqui (Mission side) to the north.

The housing is single-detached homes on acreages, working farms and estate properties — berries, vineyards, poultry and equestrian operations interwoven with the housing — overwhelmingly freehold; strata is rare to non-existent in the community. Lot sizes are acreage parcels (commonly multiple acres); small suburban lots are not the pattern.

Schools: Mt Lehman Elementary (K–5), 6381 Mt Lehman Rd, is the community school, School District 34 (Abbotsford); the community's first school opened in 1884 and schooling has been continuous on the site since. Feeder pattern (resolved): SD34's Eugene Reimer Middle "Family of Schools" page lists Mt. Lehman Elementary among the schools whose students attend Reimer beginning grade 6, and names Rick Hansen Secondary (9–12) as that family's secondary school — pathway: Mt Lehman Elementary → Eugene Reimer Middle → Rick Hansen Secondary. Confirm any individual address in SD34's School Locator.

Community anchors: Mount Lehman Hall, 6418 Mount Lehman Road, built in 1904, operated by the Mount Lehman Community Association (formed 1990), hosts the Annual Fall Fair, Country Market and Canada Day parade. The City owns and operates four cemeteries, one being Mt. Lehman Cemetery on Taylor Road. Heritage caution: the City's published Community Heritage Register list contains no Mount Lehman building (hall, church, Taylor House or cemetery) and only register sites carry that status — the village buildings are historic but not register-listed or designated, and must not be marketed as "heritage-registered." Fire protection is Abbotsford Fire Rescue Service Fire Hall 5 (Mt. Lehman), 30373 Merryfield Avenue.

Wineries (verified on each winery's own site): Singletree Winery, 5782 Mt. Lehman Road (family Etsell winery; tasting room Wed–Sun, 12:00 noon–5:30 pm); Seaside Pearl Farmgate Winery, 5290 Olund Road ("in beautiful Mount Lehman, Abbotsford," licence no. 307057); and Mt. Lehman Winery (family-owned boutique winery; existence own-site-confirmed — its street address was not rendered on the homepage fetched pass: Not verified from its own site).

Transit: effectively car-dependent, but not unserved. BC Transit's Central Fraser Valley Route 21 Aldergrove / Abbotsford runs Bourquin Exchange ↔ Aldergrove via Highstreet Exchange and Mt Lehman Road's south end, with 21A variants via the Abbotsford airport area; roughly hourly weekdays, reduced weekends. A new five-bay Highstreet transit exchange opened September 6, 2026, to serve "growing neighbourhoods in the Mt. Lehman area." No route runs to the village core — residents drive to a stop. Commute: Mt Lehman Road connects south to Highway 1 via interchanges in Abbotsford/Langley and north toward the Fraser River/Mission side via Matsqui; timed drives not verified.

Flood frame: Mt Lehman itself is upland — a plateau above the surrounding prairie, which is why it escaped the prairie flood profile — but it is ringed by ALR farmland and sits above Matsqui Prairie's diked floodplain. The lowland at the plateau's foot is protected by the Matsqui Dike (Province's dike inventory: City-administered, 11.3 km, 4 pump stations, 2 flood boxes, serving 4,370 ha), with over $19 million of joint Canada/BC/City bank-erosion investment announced for it. The November 2021 disaster was a Sumas Prairie event (Nooksack overflow, Sumas dike breach, over 1,100 properties evacuated) — not a Mt Lehman event.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Mt Lehman

items.t: Farm class (BC Assessment) — thresholds in full three-tier form: Class 9, Farm classification requires production of qualifying primary agricultural products for sale, with income thresholds of $2,500 (parcels 0.8–4 ha), $2,500 plus 5% of the land's value over 4 ha (parcels over 4 ha), and $10,000 (parcels under 0.8 ha), with applications due by October 31. Farm buildings are Class 1, and 50% of Class 9 land's assessed value is exempt from school taxes. Farm class is earned by production, not automatic on ALR land.

Form B diligence (strata frame — for the nearest strata purchases): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It has no in-community application today (no in-community strata stock); it is the document that would govern an Eden Court purchase (confirming the listing-described 55+ rule and pet position) and any urban Abbotsford townhouse purchase.

City plan — CURRENT, with the stale framing flagged: Abbotsford's Official Community Plan is Abbotsforward 2050, adopted December 2025 and now being implemented; it guides the rural areas' protection of agriculture and directs growth to Abbotsford's urban centres, not the rural villages.

Suites and coach/garden suites (Abbotsford's rules — this city's rules only): Abbotsford caps a secondary suite at under 50% of the principal dwelling, and caps a coach house / garden suite at 15% of the lot area to a maximum of 100 m². On ALR parcels the ALC frame above also applies (a suite only inside the principal residence), so both regimes must clear before a suite is promised on a farm parcel.

Abbotsford property taxes (2026): current-year rates are set by Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026, per $1,000 of taxable assessed value by property class. All City of Abbotsford property taxes were due July 2, 2026 by midnight; a first 5% penalty applied July 3, 2026 (including any unclaimed Home Owner Grant) and a second 5% penalty applied September 16, 2026; penalties are legislated and cannot be waived. Area-specific charges (e.g., prairie dyking districts) can appear on parcels at the plateau's foot — check a parcel's local charges. A Mt Lehman-specific levy: none found (Not verified as a negative). Municipal water vs. well and septic vs. sewer are parcel-specific here — verify per property.

blocks.text: Good to know about Mt Lehman

items.t: "Mt Lehman" will never appear on a stats sheet. A buyer asking an agent for "the Mt Lehman townhouse report" is asking for a document that does not exist.

The road's name outruns the community. Mt Lehman Road runs from the village core (school at 6381, hall at 6418) south past the airport/Highstreet ground to Highway 1 — which is how a 55+ strata townhouse complex at number 3348, filed by the board as Abbotsford West, ends up answering "Mt Lehman townhouse" searches. Address road ≠ community.

Elevation is the pitch, and it is literal. The community's name comes from raised ground above Matsqui Prairie's diked floodplain; the November 2021 flood disaster that buyers picture was Sumas Prairie, a different prairie in the same city. Plateau-edge parcels still need their own flood check — "upland community" is not a per-lot guarantee.

The wineries are the retail. There is no retail centre in Mt Lehman — daily shopping is Abbotsford (Clearbrook/Highstreet) or Langley — but three estate wineries (Mt. Lehman, Singletree at 5782 Mt. Lehman Road, Seaside Pearl at 5290 Olund Road) are the community's farm-gate storefronts, verified on their own sites.

A transit exchange opened for a community with no village bus route. The five-bay Highstreet exchange (opened September 6, 2026) is expressly meant to serve "growing neighbourhoods in the Mt. Lehman area," and Route 21 runs the road's south end — but no route reaches the village core, so every transit trip from the plateau starts with a drive.

Farm class is earned, and the threshold is not flat. A Mt Lehman acreage does not get Class 9 farm taxes by being in the ALR: it must produce qualifying products for sale and meet the three-tier income thresholds ($2,500 / $2,500 + 5% over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by October 31).

The fire hall carries the community's name into the urban fringe. Abbotsford Fire Hall 5 (Mt. Lehman), 30373 Merryfield Avenue, serves this ground — and its address is a reminder that Mt Lehman, as a service name, stretches well south of the village core, like the road itself.

items.t: Fee-simple lots — the default and effectively only form: acreage parcels (commonly multiple acres) carrying single-detached homes, working farms and estate properties — no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees on the community's houses and farms. Small suburban lots are not the pattern, and strata is rare to non-existent in the community on the research's own statement.

The workhorse zone: Agricultural One Zone (A1) under Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014, s. 210 — intent "to accommodate Agricultural and Agri-Tourism uses on lots that are 8.0 ha and larger in size"; principal uses include Agricultural Use, Agri-Tourism, Farm Retail Sales, a Single Detached Dwelling and a Winery, plus accessory family/employee residential uses and a Secondary Suite. Any parcel's actual zone is per-parcel: check with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR split, as documented: the community is ringed by ALR farmland and most working land is A1-zoned — but the research states the exact ALR share for the community is not verified, so no percentage or parcel split is asserted here.
Assemblies/proposals: none documented — the research records "very little" new development, with growth directed to Abbotsford's urban centres under Abbotsforward 2050, not the rural villages.

The November 2021 disaster was a Sumas Prairie event (Nooksack overflow, Sumas dike breach, over 1,100 properties evacuated) — not a Mt Lehman event. Local rules that affect duplexes in Mt Lehman

items.t: Abbotsford's suite rule is a suite under 50% of the principal dwelling — this city's rule, never borrowed from another city's. Abbotsford's coach/garden suite figures (15% of lot to a maximum 100 m²) apply in Abbotsford only. On an ALR parcel, the ALC's "Housing in the ALR" package governs instead: Generally one residence per parcel unless it qualifies for an additional one; a principal residence of 500 m² or less (max 1,000 m² of fill); a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; anything beyond the permitted number/size needs ALC approval, and the City may further restrict residences. ALC Policy L-26 (amended May 2025): An additional residence beyond the regulation may only be permitted if necessary for a farm use — the farm-worker housing route.

faq.a: None verified — zero. The community's housing is freehold acreage homes, working farms and estate properties, and ALR law bars stratifying farm residences. Anyone marketing a "Mt Lehman condo" is marketing an urban Abbotsford building under a rural name.
faq.q: How many condo buildings does Mt Lehman have?

faq.a: No. ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. 21(1)); a second residence on ALR land is an accessory farm/employee residence or a suite inside the principal residence, and it conveys only with the parcel.
faq.q: Can a Mt Lehman farm's second home be sold to me separately as a condo?

faq.a: Mt Lehman buyers who need strata product are shopping a drive away, in a different sub-area.
faq.q: Where is the nearest actual condo stock?

faq.a: That is the realistic multi-household route here: A1 zoning permits a Secondary Suite as an accessory use, and on ALR land the ALC allows a secondary suite only inside the principal residence, with anything beyond the permitted number/size needing ALC approval — check the specific parcel's zone and ALR status first.
faq.q: Can I add a suite or second dwelling on a Mt Lehman acreage for family or a caregiver?

faq.a: The village itself is upland — that elevation is the origin of the "Mount" — but it is ringed by ALR farmland above Matsqui Prairie's diked floodplain, protected by the 11.3 km Matsqui Dike. Plateau-edge and prairie-floor parcels need their own flood check.
faq.q: Is Mt Lehman in the floodplain?

faq.a: None verified inside the community — 0 strata, 0 fee-simple. The housing is freehold acreage homes and farms, and on ALR land a residence cannot be stratified at all, so the product cannot be created here parcel by parcel.
faq.q: Are there any townhouses in Mt Lehman?

faq.a: A buyer can absolutely buy there — the diligence is Abbotsford West strata diligence (Form B first), not rural Mt Lehman diligence.
faq.q: What about Eden Court on Mt Lehman Road — isn't that a Mt Lehman townhouse complex?

faq.a: Not as a board sub-area — there is no Mt Lehman row. The closest published figures are Abbotsford-wide (September 2026: detached median $949,000; "Condos & Townhomes" combined median $497,500 — community figures, never Mt Lehman figures) and the neighbouring rural sub-areas (Bradner, Matsqui). Set pricing expectations from Bradner/Matsqui/Aberdeen rural comparables plus acreage sales, not a sub-area stats sheet.
faq.q: Can I find Mt Lehman market stats?

faq.a: There is no acreage subdivision or bare-land strata product to buy instead.
faq.q: What am I actually buying on a Mt Lehman acreage?

faq.a: On ALR land, no suite outside the principal residence — the ALC rule controls. Off ALR, Abbotsford's own caps apply: a suite under 50% of the principal dwelling, and a coach/garden suite at 15% of lot area to a maximum of 100 m² (Abbotsford's rules only). The parcel's ALR status decides which answer governs.
faq.q: Can I add a suite in a barn, or a coach house?

faq.a: A buyer can buy there — the diligence is Abbotsford West strata diligence (Form B first), not rural Mt Lehman diligence.
faq.q: What about Eden Court on Mt Lehman Road — isn't that Mt Lehman stock?

faq.a: A Mt Lehman purchase is a whole parcel under one title: An acreage home, a hobby farm or a working farm.
faq.q: Is there any half duplex for sale in Mt Lehman?

faq.a: On ALR land the ALC package governs: A secondary suite only inside the principal residence as-of-right, and an additional residence only through the farm-use route (Policy L-26) or ALC approval. Off ALR, Abbotsford's suite rule (under 50% of the principal dwelling) and the zoning govern. Confirm per lot.
